claims.text: A business objective is a specific goal, stated so that progress towards it can be measured, that an organisation sets itself to reach within a stated period.

claims.text: The objectives an organisation sets follow from who owns it and what it exists to do, which is why private sector businesses, public sector organisations and social enterprises tend to set different objectives.

verification.method: Authored 2026-09-12 under standard v0.2.0-draft against the 9609 v2 syllabus scope for topic 1.4. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Organisations in all three sectors need enough revenue to cover their costs; what separates them is what any surplus is for - a return to private owners, the continued funding of a public service, or reinvestment in a social purpose.

verification.method: Authored 2026-09-12 under standard v0.2.0-draft against the 9609 v2 syllabus scope for topic 1.4. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The private sector is the part of the economy owned by private individuals and shareholders rather than by the state, and the objectives of a private sector business are set by those owners.

verification.method: Authored 2026-09-12 under standard v0.2.0-draft against the 9609 v2 syllabus scope for topic 1.4. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Objectives commonly set by private sector businesses include survival, profit maximisation, profit satisficing, growth in sales or market share, increasing the value of the owners' shareholding, and personal independence for an owner-manager.

claims.text: Survival tends to be the leading objective for a new business or for one whose sales have fallen sharply, because a business that runs out of cash has to stop trading whatever else it was aiming at.

claims.text: Profit maximisation means aiming for the largest profit the business can earn; profit satisficing means aiming for a profit good enough to satisfy the owners while other things they value - free time, independence, keeping control - are also served.

claims.text: The public sector is the part of the economy owned and controlled by national or local government on behalf of the public, and the objectives of a public sector organisation are set within government policy rather than by private owners.

verification.method: Authored 2026-09-12 under standard v0.2.0-draft against the 9609 v2 syllabus scope for topic 1.4. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Objectives commonly set for public sector organisations include supplying a service to everyone entitled to it, meeting stated standards of quality and access, staying within the budget allocated to them, and supporting wider social aims such as employment or the development of a particular region.

claims.text: A public sector organisation is usually asked to cover its costs, or to earn a stated return, rather than to maximise profit, because its owner is the state and the reason it exists is the service rather than the surplus.

claims.text: Because a public sector organisation answers to government and ultimately to taxpayers, value for money - the amount and quality of service obtained for the money spent - is usually one of the measures applied to it.
